evals.prompt: our CLAUDE.md feels really bloated and Claude keeps ignoring half of what's in it. can you clean it up? repo root has CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md
evals.expected_output: Findings-first review that flags: the doc is well over the ~200-line CLAUDE.md target (now genuinely ~208 lines after padding the fixture); large chunks (directory layout, dependency list, generic architecture overview, onboarding checklist, FAQ, glossary) are derivable or belong elsewhere and should be trimmed or relocated; the multi-step deploy playbook is a workflow, not a standing fact, and belongs in a skill or on-demand doc, not an always-loaded CLAUDE.md; CLAUDE.local.md duplicates several lines verbatim from CLAUDE.md (build/test commands) that should live in one place only. The 4 pitfalls (Stripe webhook signature ordering, enum migration transaction, Redis TTL dedup, fixture customer UUID) and the coding conventions are kept since the agent couldn't derive them from the codebase alone. Applies fixes after presenting findings.
expectations: Flags CLAUDE.md as exceeding the ~200-line CLAUDE.md size guidance
Identifies derivable content (directory layout, dependency list, or architecture overview) as a leanness/trim candidate
Flags the multi-step deploy playbook as a workflow that belongs in a skill or on-demand doc rather than an always-loaded CLAUDE.md
Flags verbatim duplication of the build/test commands between CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md
Preserves the 4 project-specific pitfalls (Stripe webhook signature ordering, enum migration transaction flag, Redis TTL dedup, fixture customer UUID) rather than deleting them
Presents findings before applying edits

evals.prompt: our AI coding tools keep behaving differently depending on which one runs on this repo -- can you check our CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and cursor rules and make them consistent? repo root has CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and .cursor/rules/testing.mdc
evals.expected_output: Findings-first review that surfaces the direct contradiction between CLAUDE.md ('mock all external services in every test, including integration tests, with no exceptions') and .cursor/rules/testing.mdc ('never mock the database in integration tests under src/payments/'), resolves it by scope (the narrower, path-scoped cursor rule for src/payments/ wins over the repo-wide CLAUDE.md guidance for that area, rather than picking one arbitrarily or just asking the user), and flags terminology drift referring to the AI itself as 'the agent' (CLAUDE.md), 'the assistant' (AGENTS.md), and 'Claude' (AGENTS.md commit-style section, cursor rule) inconsistently across the corpus. Should present findings ranked by severity before editing.
expectations: Identifies the direct contradiction between CLAUDE.md's 'mock all external services, no exceptions' and .cursor/rules/testing.mdc's 'never mock the database ... under src/payments/'
Resolves the contradiction by scope (the narrower, path-scoped cursor rule wins for src/payments/) rather than treating it as a tie needing a user decision
Flags terminology drift referring to the AI itself as 'the agent' / 'the assistant' / 'Claude' inconsistently across CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and the cursor rule
References content from all three files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .cursor/rules/testing.mdc) in the findings, not just one
Presents findings ranked by severity (blocking/should-fix/nit or equivalent tiers) rather than as a flat list

evals.prompt: can you tidy up my CLAUDE.md, it's a bit of a mess
evals.expected_output: Even though the user named only CLAUDE.md, the skill notices and reads the neighboring .clinerules and .windsurfrules files in the same repo root, and flags that 3 of CLAUDE.md's 5 conventions are duplicated verbatim in .clinerules (black formatting, pytest-before-PR, Conventional Commits) and 1 in .windsurfrules (reversible migrations) as a duplication finding across the corpus -- rather than only reviewing CLAUDE.md in isolation.
expectations: Discovers and reads the neighboring .clinerules and .windsurfrules files even though the user named only CLAUDE.md
Flags verbatim duplication of at least 3 rules between CLAUDE.md and .clinerules (black formatting, pytest-before-PR, Conventional Commits)
Flags verbatim duplication of the reversible-migrations rule between CLAUDE.md and .windsurfrules
Findings discuss the content of the other files, not just their existence

evals.prompt: our CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md have both grown and I can't tell what in them is actually doing any work any more -- can you go through both and cut what isn't? repo root has CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md
evals.expected_output: Fixture: a root CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md, both under their size ceilings, where the waste is meaning rather than length. Paraphrased cross-doc duplication, no two wordings matching verbatim: CLAUDE.md 'Run the full suite with `pytest -q` before opening a pull request' against AGENTS.md 'No PR goes up until `pytest -q` passes locally'; CLAUDE.md 'Every database migration must be reversible -- always write the down step' against AGENTS.md 'Migrations need a rollback path; don't ship one you can't undo'. Within-doc restatement: CLAUDE.md states the Conventional Commits rule once under a 'Commits' heading and again in a 'Before you push' checklist. No-ops: 'Write clean, readable code', 'Follow industry best practices', 'Think carefully before making changes', 'Be careful when editing files', 'Add comments where appropriate'. A prohibition wall in AGENTS.md: 'Never use `print` for logging. Never commit secrets. Never edit files under `generated/`' -- the last of which has an obvious positive target, regenerating via `make codegen`. Keepers the agent cannot derive or already know: the `orders_v2` `status` Postgres enum needing its own migration outside a transaction, and `make seed` being required before the integration tests or the fixture tenant is missing. Findings-first review that flags the two paraphrase pairs as duplication despite the differing wording, the Conventional Commits rule as duplicated within one doc, and the no-op lines as changing no behavior -- then deletes the no-ops outright rather than tightening their prose, rewrites the `generated/` rule around its positive target, keeps both pitfalls, and does not treat the docs as clean merely because both sit under their size ceilings.
expectations: Flags the pytest-before-PR rule as duplicated between CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md even though the two wordings do not match verbatim
Flags the reversible-migration rule as duplicated between CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md even though the two wordings do not match verbatim
Flags the Conventional Commits rule as restated twice within CLAUDE.md alone, not only across the two docs

Flags at least three of the no-op lines ('Write clean, readable code', 'Follow industry best practices', 'Think carefully before making changes', 'Be careful when editing files', 'Add comments where appropriate') as changing no behavior versus the plain model
Deletes the no-op lines outright rather than rewording, tightening, or merging them into other sections
Rewrites the 'never edit files under generated/' prohibition around its positive target (regenerate via `make codegen`) instead of leaving a bare prohibition
Preserves the two project-specific pitfalls (the orders_v2 enum migration outside a transaction, and `make seed` before the integration tests)
Does not report the docs as sound on the grounds that both are under their format's size ceiling
Presents findings before applying edits
